blocking.title: The required pi sentence is false for a 2xx answer: pi's Codex refresh does not use .catch on a 2xx body
blocking.detail: The sentence the main loop dictated appears 8 times in ADR-0251, once in the decisions README row, once in providers-and-models.md and its bundled copy, and wrapped in the CHANGELOG, the StatusBeforeBody docstring and the commit message. It reads: 'For an answer whose body fails mid-read, ... (its Codex refresh reads such a body with .catch, ...)'. 'Such a body' covers a 2xx too. In pi @ 1cedd3272 (openai-codex.ts readTokenResponse), the .catch sits inside 'if (!response.ok)' (:123-125). A 2xx is read with an uncaught 'await response.json()' (:128). So the parenthetical over-generalises pi's .catch, the same kind of error verify r5 blocked on. ADR 12.3's own 'source facts' line already says it precisely: 'a failed answer's body'. The lane applied the dictated wording verbatim, so the main loop owns the fix. Minimal fix, applied in every copy: 'its Codex refresh reads a non-2xx answer's body with .catch, its Anthropic and Copilot refreshes do not'.
blocking.evidence: I ran pi's real refresh code against my own raw-socket recorder in both framings (.omc/probes/379-live/r7verify/logs/pi_probe.out). At Codex, tr200, tk200, ck200, gz200, gk200, sl200 and sk200 all let the body error escape ('terminated' or 'The operation was aborted due to timeout'), and isRetryableAssistantError retried it. tr401, tk401, ck401, gz401, gk401, sl401 and sk401 gave '(401): Status', which is the .catch path, so the .catch applies to non-2xx answers only. Source: /tmp/pi-1cedd3272/packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/openai-codex.ts:123-128.
